rows.short_title: New York City Indirect Source Rule 'WISER' Program
rows.additional_description_1:
New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) proposes to implement a Warehouse Indirect Source Emissions Reduction (WISER) local law that would require large warehouse operators to reduce mobile sources of pollution and/or mitigate the impact of the air pollution associated with their operations in New York City. In accordance with the State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) (Section 8-0113, Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law) as set forth in 6 NYCRR Part 617, and the City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR) process, as set forth in Executive Order 91 of 1977 and its amendments, DEP is hereby issuing Notice of Positive Declaration, Intent to Prepare a Draft Environmental Impact Statement, Lead Agency Declaration and Draft Scope of Work.

DEP will hold a virtual public scoping meeting to receive public comments on the Draft Scope of Work on November 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The Draft Scope of Work, which provides a summary description of the Program and the methodologies to be used in preparing the Draft EIS impact analyses, is available on the DEP website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/about/environmental-reviews.page. You may register for the virtual public meeting at: https://bit.ly/4egU5lY. Comments on the Draft Scope of Work may be presented at the meeting or submitted in writing or by email to:

Dana Taplin, Project Manager

NYC Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Environmental Planning and Analysis

59-17 Junction Boulevard, 4th Floor

Flushing, NY 11373

dtaplin@dep.nyc.gov

Written comments on the Draft Scope of Work will be accepted until December 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. DEP will subsequently issue a Final Scope of Work, which will include responses to written comments and comments received during the public meeting and may incorporate revisions in response to comments received.

New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) proposes to implement a Warehouse Indirect Source Emissions Reduction (WISER) local law that would require large warehouse operators to reduce mobile sources of pollution and/or mitigate the impact of the air pollution associated with their operations in New York City. In accordance with the State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) (Section 8-0113, Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law) as set forth in 6 NYCRR Part 617, and the City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR) process, as set forth in Executive Order 91 of 1977 and its amendments, DEP is hereby issuing Notice of Positive Declaration, Intent to Prepare a Draft Environmental Impact Statement, Lead Agency Declaration and Draft Scope of Work.

DEP will hold a virtual public scoping meeting to receive public comments on the Draft Scope of Work on November 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The Draft Scope of Work, which provides a summary description of the Program and the methodologies to be used in preparing the Draft EIS impact analyses, is available on the DEP website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/about/environmental-reviews.page. NYC Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Environmental Planning and Analysis

59-17 Junction Boulevard, 4th Floor

Flushing, NY 11373

dtaplin@dep.nyc.gov

Written comments on the Draft Scope of Work will be accepted until December 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on November 10, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed disposition of the real property identified below. The public hearing will be held via conference call. Call in #1-646-992-2010; Access code: 2342 243 5265

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of The Bronx:

 

Address                                                                          Block/Lot(s)

 

501 West 174th Street                                                       2131/50

511 West 171st Street                                                       2128/55

522 West 174th Street                                                       2130/39

         

Under HPD's Affordable Neighborhood Cooperative Program, occupied City-owned residential buildings are purchased by Restoring Communities Housing Development Fund Corporation (Sponsor) and then rehabilitated by a private developer selected through a request for qualifications.  Upon conveyance to the Sponsor, buildings will be managed by the private developers.  Following completion of rehabilitation, Sponsor conveys the building to a cooperative housing development fund corporation (Cooperative Corporation) formed by the buildings tenants.  The cooperative interests attributable to occupied apartments will be sold to the existing tenants for $2,500 per apartment.  The cooperative interests attributable to vacant apartments will be sold for a price affordable to families earning no more than 165% of the area median income.

 

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Sponsor for the nominal price of one dollar per building.  When completed, the project will provide 50 affordable cooperative dwelling units.

 

At the time of sale, the Sponsor will be required to sign a rental regulatory agreement with HPD containing, among other things, restrictions on rents, incomes, and assets.  When the Sponsor conveys the building to the Cooperative Corporation upon the completion of rehabilitation, the Cooperative Corporation will be required to sign a cooperative regulatory agreement with HPD containing, among other things, restrictions on sale prices, incomes, and assets as well as requirements for a flip tax and building reserve fund.

 

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

 

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, PURSUANT TO LAW, that the following proposed revocable consent has been scheduled for a public hearing by the New York City Department of Transportation. A draft copy of the revocable consent agreement(s) may be obtained at no cost by submitting a request at diningoutnyc.info/requestcopy

The public hearing will be held remotely via Zoom, commencing on October 29th, 2026, at 11:00 am, in the matter of a proposed revocable consent authorizing the following:

  1. ARIARI NYC LLC to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 119 1st Avenue in the Borough of Manhattan.

  2. COZY CORNER CORP to maintain, operate and use a sidewalk cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 60-01 70 Avenue in the Borough of Queens.

rows.short_title: FOR LEASE - 105 East 106th Street & 104 East 107th Street
rows.additional_description_1:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN THAT A REAL PROPERTY ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSITIONS PUBLIC HEARING, in accordance with Section 824 of the New York City Charter, will be held on October 28, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. via Conference Call No. 1-646-992-2010, Access Code 717 876 299.

 

IN THE MATTER OF a renewal of the lease for the City of New York, as tenant, on the entire fourth and fifth floors of the building located at  105 East 106th Street (Block 1634 & Lot 3), and on the partial fourth floor of the building located at 104 East 107th Street (Block 1634 & Lot 65) in the Borough of Manhattan for the Emergency Hazardous Services and Emergency Repair Services divisions  of the Department of Housing Preservation and Development to use as an office, or for such other use as the Commissioner of the Department of Citywide Administrative Services may determine.

 

The proposed use was approved by the City Planning Commission pursuant to NYC Charter Section 195c on February 19, 1992 (CPC Appl. No. N 920296 PXM, Public Hearing Cal. No. 7).

 

The proposed renewal of the lease shall commence on full lease execution and shall expire on the earlier of (i) twenty (20) years after the Substantial Completion Date, or (ii) twenty-one (21) years after the Commencement Date, at an annual rent of $1,086,960.00 from Lease Execution through Substantial Completion Date, $1,168,482.00 from Substantial Completion Date through the first five (5) years, $1,304,352.00 for the following five (5) years, $1,440,222.00 for the following five (5) years, and $1,576,092.00 for the last five (5) years, payable in equal monthly installments at the end of each month.

 

The lease may be terminated by the Tenant in its entirety at the end of twelfth (12) year from the Commencement Date, provided the Tenant gives the Landlord twelve (12) months prior written notice.  In the event that the lease is terminated by the Tenant, the Tenant shall pay to the Landlord the unamortized portion of both Landlords cost of the alterations, improvements and such portion of the commission paid to Tenant Representative Broker.

 

The Landlord shall prepare final architectural plans and engineering plans and make alterations and improvements in accordance with preliminary architectural plans and specifications which are attached to the lease.  The alterations and improvements consist of Base Building Work, which the Landlord shall provide at its sole cost and expense.

 

Further information, including public inspection of the proposed lease, may be obtained, at One Centre Street, Room 2000 North, New York, NY. 10007. To schedule an inspection, please email RESPublicHearingInquiries@dcas.nyc.gov

 

If you need further accommodations, please let us know at least five business days in advance of the Public Hearing via email at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at 212-298-0734.

In the event that the lease is terminated by the Tenant, the Tenant shall pay to the Landlord the unamortized portion of both Landlords cost of the alterations, improvements and such portion of the commission paid to Tenant Representative Broker.

The Landlord shall prepare final architectural plans and engineering plans and make alterations and improvements in accordance with preliminary architectural plans and specifications which are attached to the lease. The alterations and improvements consist of Base Building Work, which the Landlord shall provide at its sole cost and expense.

Further information, including public inspection of the proposed lease, may be obtained, at One Centre Street, Room 2000 North, New York, NY. 10007. To schedule an inspection, please email RESPublicHearingInquiries@dcas.nyc.gov

If you need further accommodations, please let us know at least five business days in advance of the Public Hearing via email at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at 212-298-0734.

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 22, 2026 at the 224 West 124th Street Library, Manhattan, at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

              Address                      Block/Lots            Community District

              53 East 110 Street             1616/123             11

              304 East 126 Street           1802/47               11

              201 East 120 Street           1785/1                 11

              204 West 121 Street          1926/35               10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.                                                                                                      

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010. TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010. TDD users should call Verizon relay services. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the following matters have been scheduled for Public Hearing by Community Board:

 BOROUGH OF BROOKLYN

COMMUNITY BOARD NO. 18 Wednesday, October 21, 2026, 7:00 pm, Board Office Meeting Room, 1097 Bergen Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11234 and via Zoom for participants who wish to participate online.  

  • ULURP Application #C250145MMK (East 56th Street Demapping)  Premises affected  5601 Kingsway Place, 709 East 56th Street, 5379 Preston Court, Kingsway Place, East 56th Street.  An application submitted by Captain Holdings Corp. for a City Map amendment to demap an approximately 20,578-square-foot portion of East 56th Street between Brooklyn Block 7932 and Block 7949, north of Preston Court and south of the LIRR Bay Ridge Branch. The proposed action would facilitate the reconfiguration of an existing school bus parking facility and the development of two single-story office trailers, providing approximately 121 bus parking spaces and 42 accessory off-street parking spaces in the East Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn Community District 18. This Statutory Public Hearing has been duly advertised in the City Record.

rows.short_title: New York City Housing Authority Board Meeting
rows.additional_description_1:
The next Board Meeting of the New York City Housing Authority is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. in the Ceremonial Room on the 5th Floor of 90 Church Street, New York, New York 10007 (unless otherwise noted). This Board Meeting will also be streamed live on NYCHA's YouTube Channel at https://www.youtube.com/c/nycha and NYCHA's Website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/board-meetings.page

These Board Meetings are open to the public. To provide comment in-person, all speakers are required to pre-register, at least forty-five (45) minutes before the scheduled Board Meeting. Comments are limited to the items on the Calendar. Speaking time will be limited to three (3) minutes. The public comment period will conclude upon all speakers being heard or at the expiration of thirty (30) minutes allotted for public comment, whichever occurs first. Comments may also be provided to the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by mail at 90 Church Street, 5th Floor, New York NY 10007.

Please note that the Minutes for prior Board Meetings and the Calendar for the upcoming Board Meeting may be obtained by visiting the NYCHA Website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/board-meetings.page. Copies of the Calendar may also be picked up at the Office of the Corporate Secretary at 90 Church Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY, 10007, no earlier than twenty-four (24) hours before the upcoming Board Meeting. Copies of the Draft Minutes may also be picked up at the Office of the Corporate Secretary, no earlier than 3:00 P.M. on the Tuesday following the Board Meeting. Any changes to the schedule will be posted on this webpage and via social media, to the extent practicable, at a reasonable time before the Board Meeting.

Any person requiring a reasonable accommodation, including wheelchair accessibility or large print availability, to participate in the Board Meeting should contact the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by phone at (212) 306-6088, no later than 5:00 P.M., seven (7) calendar days before the Board Meeting.

For additional information regarding Board Meetings, please contact the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by phone at (212) 306-6088.

rows.additional_description_1:
Design Commission Meeting Agenda 

Tuesday, October 20, 2026 

 

Meeting Location: Public Design Commission meetings are being held in-person at the Public Design Commission Board Room on the 3rd floor of City Hall. Members of the public can attend and give testimony either in-person or remotely. The entrance to City Hall, restrooms, and the boardroom are wheelchair accessible. 

 

To attend or testify remotely, the public can join the meeting via Microsoft Teams at https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/236451131020192?p=hxYhjUCPABZJsDJ5GV or by calling +1 332-910-6701 and using the phone conference ID: 103 902 010#. 

 

Members of the public who wish to give testimony on public hearing items can sign-up in advance using this form: https://tinyurl.com/PDCmeetingform. Instructions for testifying remotely via Microsoft Teams or by phone can be found on our website here: https://tinyurl.com/PDC-testimony-teams. 

 

The meeting will be livestreamed on the Public Design Commissions YouTube channel at http://www.youtube.com/nycdesigncommission.  

 

 

Public Meeting 

 

9:20 a.m. Consent Items 

 

30559: Renovation of Pacific Library, including the construction of an addition and garden, 25 Fourth Avenue, Brooklyn. (Preliminary) (CC 39, CB 6) BPL 

 

30560: Reinstallation of four artworks by Clemente Spampinato, Walt Whitman Library, 93 Saint Edwards Street, Brooklyn. (Final) (CC 35, CB 2) BPL 

 

30561: Reconstruction of the trail (South Forest Riverwalk), including construction of seating areas and ADA accessible pathways, New York Botanical Garden, River Road and East Fordham Road, Bronx. (Final) (CC 11, CB 7) DCLA/DPR 

 

30562: Construction of a housing facility, Crossroads Juvenile Center, 17 Bristol Street, Brooklyn. (Final) (CC 41, CB 16) DDC/ACS 

 

30563: Construction of streetscape improvements, including reconstruction of a median, Bay 37th Street, Harway Avenue, Bay 38th Street, and Cropsey Avenue, and construction of a plaza, Kenilworth Place, Hillel Place, Flatbush Avenue, and Nostrand Avenue, Brooklyn. (Preliminary) (CC 45 & 47, CB 11 & 14) DDC/DOT 

 

30564: Reconstruction of a step street (Library Lane), Coles Lane between Kingsbridge Road and Bainbridge Avenue, Bronx. (Final) (CC 15, CB 7) DDC/DOT 

 

30565: Minor modifications to the construction of a public restroom building and adjacent site work, Kissena Park, Parsons Boulevard and Booth Memorial Avenue, Flushing, Queens. (Amended Final) (CC 20, CB 7) DDC/DPR 

 

30566: Installation of real time passenger information signage as part of the design of a prototypical bus shelter for installation citywide. (Amended Final) DOT 

 

30567: Modifications to the construction of an open space (The Baseline) under the ramps to the Ed Koch Queensborough Bridge, Dutch Kills Street between Jackson Avenue and the Long Island Rail Road, Long Island City, Queens. (Amended Final) (CC 26, CB 2) DOT 

 

30568: Construction of shared-use pathways and trails, West 172nd Street and West 181st Street, adjacent to Henry Hudson Parkway, Fort Washington Park, Manhattan. (Preliminary) (CC 10, CB 12) DPR 

 

30569: Reconstruction of a multipurpose play area, Sunrise Playground, adjacent to P.S. 195, 253rd Street between 149th Avenue and 149th Road, Rosedale, Queens. (Preliminary) (CC 31, CB 13) DPR 

 

30570: Construction of a broadcasting facility, including the construction of an addition?to an existing broadcasting facility and adjacent site work, United States Tennis Association's Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Flushing, Queens. (Preliminary and Final) (CC 21 & 24, CB 3, 4, 6 & 7) DPR 

 

30571: Reconstruction of Twenty-Four Sycamores Park, East 61st Street, FDR Drive, East 60th Street, and York Avenue, Manhattan. (Final) (CC 5, CB 8) DPR 

 

30572: Conservation of the Kimlau War Memorial (1962) by Poy G. Lee, Park Row and Chatham Square, Frankfort Street to Catherine Street, Manhattan. (Final) (CC 1, CB 3) DPR 

 

30573: Reconstruction of the northeastern portion of Ferry Point Park, including the reconstruction of the detention basin and sports courts, Balcom Avenue between Schley Avenue and Miles Avenue, Bronx. (Preliminary) (CC 13, CB 10) DPR/DOT 

 

30574: Modifications to a serpentine bench, as part of the reconstruction of Damrosch Park, including streetscape improvements, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, West 62nd Street between Columbus Avenue and Amsterdam Avenue, Manhattan. (Amended Final) (CC 6, CB 7) DPR/DOT 

 

30575: Installation of a security toll booth and gates, Hunts Point Cooperative Market, 355 Food Center Drive, Bronx. (Preliminary) (CC 17, CB 2) EDC 

 

30576: Construction of an electrical enclosure and electric vehicle chargers, municipal parking lot adjacent to Pier 11, 49 South Street, under the FDR Drive, Manhattan. (Preliminary) (CC 1, CB 3) EDC 

 

30577: Rehabilitation of a pier and bulkhead, Pier 4, Brooklyn Army Terminal, 58th Street and First Avenue, Brooklyn. (Preliminary and Final) (CC 38, CB 7) EDC 

 

30578: Installation of building identification signage, Atlantic Center, 625 Atlantic Avenue, Brooklyn. (Preliminary and Final) (CC 35, CB 2) EDC 

 

30579: Installation of the Alice of Wonderland Visiting New York mural series, including Alice Steps Out of a Book, Alice and Her Friends in the Subway, Alice and Friends at the NY Public Library, Alice and Friends at the Central Park Zoo, Alice and Friends at Coney Island, The Statue of Liberty (Flying Over), The Empire State Building, Alice Flies Over the East River Bridges, Normandie Ocean Liner, Bon Voyage, Seagull Skyline, Small Harbor Scene #1, Small Harbor Scene #2, and Alice and Her Friends Return to Their Books (1938) by Abram Champanier, Gotham Health Gouverneur Health Center, 227 Madison Street, Manhattan (Preliminary) (CC 1, CB 3) HHC 

 

30580: Long-term installation of the replication of The Statue of Liberty and Swordfish, as part of the installation of the Alice of Wonderland Visiting New York mural series, Gotham Health Gouverneur Health Center, 227 Madison Street, Manhattan. (Preliminary) (CC 1, CB 3) HHC 

 

30581: Removal and temporary storage of Presence, Healing Circles by Richard Pousette-Dart, from Gotham Health Gouverneur Health Center, 227 Madison Street, Manhattan to 55 Water Street, Manhattan. (Preliminary) (CC 1, CB 3) HHC 

 

30582: Rehabilitation of the 103rd Police Precinct, 168-02 91st Avenue, Jamaica, Queens. (Preliminary and Final) (CC 27, CB 12) NYPD 

 

30583: Reconstruction of an entrance and stair, and construction of a distinctive sidewalk, New York Public Library for the Performing Arts, 40 Lincoln Center Plaza, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, West 65th Street and Amsterdam Avenue, Manhattan. (Final) (CC 6, CB 7) NYPL/DPR/DOT 

 

 

Public Hearing 

 

9:25 a.m. 

30584: Design of electric vehicle charging stations (It's Electric) for curbside installation citywide. (Preliminary) DOT 

 

https://www.nyc.gov/assets/designcommission/downloads/pdf/pres/10-20-26-DOT-p-EV-Curbside-Charging-ItsElectric.pdf 

 

10:05 a.m. 

30585: Reconstruction of the western portion of Ferry Point Park, including the construction of a playground, sports courts, and waterfront walkways, west of Hutchinson River Parkway and Schley Avenue, Bronx. (Preliminary) (CC 13, CB 10) DPR/DOT 

 

https://www.nyc.gov/assets/designcommission/downloads/pdf/pres/10-20-26-DPR-DOT-p-FerryPointParkWest.pdf 

 

10:45 a.m. 

30586: Construction of a gaming facility, resort, retail, and events complex (Integrated Resort), as part of the master plan for the Metropolitan Park (Queens Future), north of Roosevelt Avenue, between Grand Central Parkway and Seaver Way, south of the Worlds Fair Marina, and adjacent to Citi Field, Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Corona, Queens (Preliminary) (CC 21, CB 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 & 9) EDC/DPR 

 

https://www.nyc.gov/assets/designcommission/downloads/pdf/pres/10-20-26-EDC-DPR-p-QF-IntegratedResort.pdf  

 

11:45 a.m. BREAK 

 

12:15 p.m. 

30587: Installation of A Village Grows by Fitgi Saint-Louis, Roy Wilkins Recreation Center, Roy Wilkins Park, Merrick Boulevard between 118th Road and 119th Avenue, Jamaica, Queens. (Conceptual) (CC 27, CB 12) DCLA%/DDC/DPR 

 

https://www.nyc.gov/assets/designcommission/downloads/pdf/pres/10-20-26-DCLA-pfa-DDC-DPR-c-A-Village-Grows.pdf 

 

12:55 p.m. 

30588: Installation of A Necessary Secret World by Sherrill Roland, Brooklyn Detention Complex, 275 Atlantic Avenue, Brooklyn. (Conceptual) (CC 33, CB 2) DCLA%/DDC/DOC 

 

https://www.nyc.gov/assets/designcommission/downloads/pdf/pres/10-20-26-DCLA-pfa-DDC-DOC-c-A-Necessary-Secret-World.pdf  

 

All times are approximate and subject to change without notice, and those who are testifying remotely should follow along on the livestreamed meeting on the Design Commissions YouTube channel to know when to join the meeting. If testifying at City Hall, please plan to arrive early in the event the meeting is ahead of schedule. Details on giving public testimony can be found here: https://www.nyc.gov/site/designcommission/design-review/testimony/public-testimony.page 

 

Items on the consent agenda are not presented. If you wish to testify regarding a design-related issue of a project on the consent agenda, please notify staff as soon as possible.  

 

Do you need assistance to participate in the meeting? If you need a reasonable accommodation of a disability, such as translation into a language other than English; American Sign Language Interpreting (ASL); Captioning in Real-Time (CART); or the meeting agenda in Braille, large print, or electronic format, please contact the Public Design Commission at least three business days before the meeting.  

 

Public Design Commission 
City Hall, Third Floor 
Phone: 212-788-3071 
Fax: 212-788-3086 

www.nyc.gov/designcommission
